name: Add One
description: You are given an integer $$$n$$$. You have to apply $$$m$$$ operations to it. In a single operation, you must replace every digit $$$d$$$ of the number with the decimal representation of integer $$$d + 1$$$. For example, $$$1912$$$ becomes $$$21023$$$ after applying the operation once. You have to find the length of $$$n$$$ after applying $$$m$$$ operations. Since the answer can be very large, print it modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of test cases. The only line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^9$$$) and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the initial number and the number of operations.
output_specification: For each test case output the length of the resulting number modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1513C — Add One [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
